added_lemmas.statement:
Every member of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp family satisfies the declared fixed-outcome, outcome-boundedness, predictable-randomization, propensity-range, predictable-regression, intensity-profile, and residual-profile conditions. The intensity obeys
\[
 \bar q_\star(0)=c,\qquad c/2\leq\bar q_\star(u)\leq c\leq K,
 \qquad |\bar q_\star(u)-\bar q_\star(v)|\leq L_q|u-v|.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive at every time after the profile cutoff, hence also at every time after both that cutoff and the late-ramp start; both profile discrepancies in \(G_n\) are zero, the early rare-arm term and its predictable quadratic variation are zero, and \(G_n=\Omega\). Consequently \(\bar q_\star\in\mathcal Q\), \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\), and the profile contract holds eventually with probability one.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(f(u)=c-L_qu\) and \(b=c/2\). Since the map \(x\mapsto\max\{x,b\}\) is nondecreasing and one-Lipschitz,
\[
 |\bar q_\star(u)-\bar q_\star(v)|
 =|\max\{f(u),b\}-\max\{f(v),b\}|
 \leq |f(u)-f(v)|=L_q|u-v|.
\]
Moreover \(\bar q_\star(0)=\max\{c,c/2\}=c\), and, for every \(u\in[0,1]\),
\[
 c/2\leq\bar q_\star(u)\leq c\leq K.
\]
These equations verify the anchor, bound, and Lipschitz conditions, so the definition of \(\mathcal Q\) gives \(\bar q_\star\in\mathcal Q\).

The positive-part map is one-Lipschitz, and truncation by \(M\) cannot increase distances. Hence
\[
 |g_{a_\star}(u)-g_{a_\star}(v)|\leq L_r|u-v|,
 \qquad 0\leq g_{a_\star}(u)\leq M\leq B.
\]
Therefore \(|r^\sigma(u)|\leq B\) and \(r^\sigma\) is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz; the definition of \(\mathcal R\) yields \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\). The displayed construction makes the potential outcomes fixed under randomization and gives \(|Y_{nt}^\sigma(a)|\leq M\). It also makes both regressions identically zero, hence predictable and bounded by the nonnegative constant \(M_m\). Since \(0<\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\) and \(0<\rho<1\),
\[
 0<e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\}\leq\rho<1.
\]
The required conditional assignment equality holds by the construction of the sequential law.

It remains to verify the profile event rather than assume its eventual validity. Because \(n\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil>c/\rho.
\]
For every \(t\geq\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\), the upper bound \(\bar q_\star\leq c\) then gives \(\bar q_\star(t/n)/t<\rho\), whence
\[
 t e_{nt}=\bar q_\star(t/n).
\]
Thus the propensity cap is inactive after the profile cutoff. In particular it is inactive after the maximum of that cutoff and \(\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor+1\). The construction also gives, for every \(t\),
\[
 r_{nt}(1)=Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)-m_{nt}(1)=r^\sigma(t/n),
\]
so the residual-profile discrepancy is zero.

Finally, since \(\varepsilon_n\to0\), eventually \(\varepsilon_n+1/n<a_\star\). If \(t<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\), then
\[
 t/n<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil/n\leq\varepsilon_n+1/n<a_\star,
\]
and consequently \(r_{nt}(1)=0\). Every summand of \(S_{n,\mathrm{rare}}^{\mathrm{early}}\) is then zero, so that martingale and its predictable quadratic variation are both zero. All three components in the definition of \(G_n\) therefore hold on every assignment path for all sufficiently large \(n\). Thus \(G_n=\Omega\), and \(\Pr(G_n)=1\geq1-\kappa_n\) eventually.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a member of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp family and define
\[
 m_n=\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor,
 \quad V_n=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\{A_{nt}=0\},
 \quad \eta_n^\star=\prod_{t=m_n+1}^{n}
 \left[1-\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_n=\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-
 =\frac2n\sum_{t=1}^{n}\min\{L_r(t/n-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
For every possibly randomized complete-log confidence set \(D_n=D_n(O_n,U)\), where \(U\) is independent of the experiment and has the same law under both signs, let
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
With \([z]_+=\max\{z,0\}\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(\varnothing)=0\), for every \(n\) and each sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\geq\Delta_n\}
 \geq[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), this inequality is attained within this two-sign subexperiment by a possibly randomized complete-log confidence set with maximum miscoverage at most \(\alpha\) and
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\geq\Delta_n\}
 =[\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+
\]
under either sign.

The finite separation satisfies \(\Delta_n\geq d(1-a_\star)\) and converges to that value, where
\[
 d(x)=2\int_0^x\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =\begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\leq M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Furthermore
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\omega(a_\star)=\exp\{-H(a_\star)\},
 \qquad H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du.
\]
If \(0\leq L_q\leq c/2\), then
\[
 H(a)=c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\) and \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\), then
\[
 H(a)=\begin{cases}
 (c/2)\log(1/a),&a\geq u_q,\\
 c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q),&a<u_q.
 \end{cases}
\]

Define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\leq M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
\]
and, for \(0<d<d_{\max}\),
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\leq M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a(d)=1-x(d).
\]
If \((D_n)\) is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over all experiments satisfying the declared structured assumptions, then, under each sign of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp member with start \(a(d)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\geq d\}
 \geq[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+.
\]
For every \(q'\in\mathcal Q\), \(q'(u)\geq\bar q_\star(u)\) pointwise. Thus \(\bar q_\star\) maximizes the late-void mass for every fixed start, and, together with the clipped residual, the displayed bound is the jointly optimized late-void envelope among deterministic designs \(e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,q'(t/n)/t\}\) and two-sign profiles that vanish on \([0,a]\), are bounded by \(M\), and have Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\). When \(L_q>c/2\), the intensity elbow is
\[
 d_q=d\left(1-\frac{c}{2L_q}\right).
\]
The residual elbow \(M^2/L_r\) is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\); when both elbows are interior, either ordering is possible. Exact attainment is asserted only for each selected two-sign intensity-optimized clipped-ramp subexperiment, not globally over the structured class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\). By the definition of the finite-population estimand and the two potential-outcome arrays,
\[
 \tau_n^\sigma=\frac{\sigma}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n g_{a_\star}(t/n),
 \qquad
 \Delta_n=\frac2n\sum_{t=1}^n g_{a_\star}(t/n)>0.
\]
The function \(g_{a_\star}\) is nondecreasing. On each interval \(((t-1)/n,t/n]\),
\(g_{a_\star}(u)\leq g_{a_\star}(t/n)\). Summing the resulting integral inequalities gives
\[
 2\int_0^1g_{a_\star}(u)\,du
 \leq\frac2n\sum_{t=1}^ng_{a_\star}(t/n)=\Delta_n.
\]
Because \(g_{a_\star}\) is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz, the excess of the displayed, twice-scaled right Riemann sum over the twice-scaled integral is at most \(2L_r/n\). Hence
\[
 \Delta_n\longrightarrow2\int_0^1g_{a_\star}(u)\,du
 =2\int_0^{1-a_\star}\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds.
\]
If \(L_rx\leq M\), direct integration gives \(d(x)=L_rx^2\). If \(L_rx>M\), splitting at \(s=M/L_r\) gives
\[
 d(x)=2\left\{\int_0^{M/L_r}L_rs\,ds+
 \int_{M/L_r}^xM\,ds\right\}
 =2Mx-M^2/L_r.
\]
This proves the finite lower bound, the limit, and the two branches of \(d\).

We next prove the exact information inequality. The propensity sequence is deterministic and common to the two signs. Iterated conditioning under the assignment law therefore shows that its joint assignment mass is the product of the Bernoulli factors. Consequently
\[
 \Pr_\sigma(V_n)=\prod_{t=m_n+1}^n(1-e_{nt})=\eta_n^\star
\]
for both signs. For \(t\leq m_n\), one has \(t/n\leq a_\star\), so both potential outcomes are zero. On \(V_n\), every later observed treated-arm contribution is also zero. Thus the restrictions of the two augmented laws of \((O_n,U)\) to \(V_n\) coincide. Denote this common subprobability measure by \(\mu_n\); it has mass \(\eta_n^\star\).

Let \(E_\sigma=\{\tau_n^\sigma\in D_n\}\) and \(L_n=\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\geq\Delta_n\}\). If both \(E_+\) and \(E_-\) occur, the set contains two points separated by \(\Delta_n\), and therefore \(E_+\cap E_-\subseteq L_n\). Inclusion--exclusion under \(\mu_n\), followed by domination by the corresponding full laws, yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr_\sigma(L_n)&\geq\mu_n(L_n)\\
 &\geq\mu_n(E_+\cap E_-)\\
 &\geq\eta_n^\star-\mu_n(E_+^c)-\mu_n(E_-^c)\\
 &\geq\eta_n^\star-
 \Pr_+(E_+^c)-\Pr_-(E_-^c)
 \geq\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The left side is nonnegative, proving the positive-part version.

The bound is exactly attainable within the fixed pair. Outside \(V_n\), the first treated unit after \(m_n\) has nonzero observed outcome whose sign identifies \(\sigma\); report the corresponding true singleton. On \(V_n\), use the common auxiliary randomizer. Since \(e_{nt}<1\), one has \(\eta_n^\star>0\), so the following unconditional masses divided by \(\eta_n^\star\) are valid conditional randomization probabilities. If \(\eta_n^\star>2\alpha\), allocate unconditional void masses \(\alpha\), \(\alpha\), and \(\eta_n^\star-2\alpha\) to \(\{\tau_n^+\}\), \(\{\tau_n^-\}\), and \(\{\tau_n^+,\tau_n^-\}\), respectively. If \(\alpha<\eta_n^\star\leq2\alpha\), allocate unconditional void mass \(\eta_n^\star-\alpha\) to each singleton and \(2\alpha-\eta_n^\star\) to the empty set. If \(\eta_n^\star\leq\alpha\), report the empty set throughout \(V_n\). These masses are nonnegative and sum to \(\eta_n^\star\) in every case. Under either sign, the void-event miscoverage is at most \(\alpha\), and the only output having diameter \(\Delta_n\) is the two-target set in the first case. Therefore
\[
 \max_\sigma\Pr_\sigma(E_\sigma^c)\leq\alpha,
 \qquad
 \Pr_\sigma(L_n)=[\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+.
\]

For the void limit, fix \(a=a_\star>0\). Since \(m_n+1\geq an\) and \(\bar q_\star\leq c\), the cap is inactive for every \(t>m_n\) once \(n\) is large. Put \(z_{nt}=\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\). Uniformly over the retained indices, \(z_{nt}=O(n^{-1})\); hence, using \(|\log(1-z)+z|\leq z^2/(1-z)\) for \(0\leq z<1\),
\[
 \left|\log\eta_n^\star+
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^nz_{nt}\right|
 \leq\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n\frac{z_{nt}^2}{1-z_{nt}}
 =O(n^{-1})\longrightarrow0.
\]
The function \(u\mapsto\bar q_\star(u)/u\) is continuous on \([a,1]\), and
\[
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^nz_{nt}
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n
 \frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}{t/n}
 \longrightarrow\int_a^1\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du=H(a).
\]
Exponentiation gives \(\eta_n^\star\to\exp\{-H(a)\}\).

If \(0\leq L_q\leq c/2\), then \(c-L_qu\geq c/2\) on \([0,1]\), so
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1(c/u-L_q)\,du
 =c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\), the affine part meets the floor at \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\in(0,1)\). For \(a\geq u_q\), the intensity equals \(c/2\) throughout \([a,1]\), giving \(H(a)=(c/2)\log(1/a)\). For \(a<u_q\), splitting at \(u_q\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H(a)
 &=\int_a^{u_q}(c/u-L_q)\,du+
 \int_{u_q}^1\frac{c}{2u}\,du\\
 &=c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q).
 \end{aligned}
\]

We now invert the residual separation. The function \(d\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,1]\), with
\[
 d(1)=\begin{cases}L_r,&L_r\leq M,\\2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}=d_{\max}.
\]
If \(L_r\leq M\), every \(d<d_{\max}\) is on the quadratic branch. If \(L_r>M\), the clipping point \(x=M/L_r\) is interior and its image is \(M^2/L_r\). Solving the two branch equations gives exactly the displayed \(x(d)\); in all cases
\[
 0<x(d)<1,qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1),qquad d(x(d))=d.
\]

Fix this selected pair. Its membership in the structured class is supplied by the membership proposition. Uniform asymptotic honesty implies
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\leq\alpha.
\]
Since \(\Delta_n\geq d(x(d))=d\), the finite information inequality and continuity of \(z\mapsto[z]_+\) imply, for each sign,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\geq d\}
 &\geq\liminf_{n\to\infty}[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+\\
 &\geq[\exp\{-H(a(d))\}-2\alpha]_+.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For the matching pair-specific construction, the only positive-diameter output is the two-target set, whose diameter \(\Delta_n\) is at least \(d\). Hence its probability at threshold \(d\) is exactly \([\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+\), which converges to the displayed envelope. This is pairwise attainment only.

It remains to certify joint optimality. If \(q'\in\mathcal Q\), the anchor and Lipschitz conditions give
\[
 q'(u)\geq q'(0)-L_qu=c-L_qu,
\]
while the intensity lower bound gives \(q'(u)\geq c/2\). Therefore
\[
 q'(u)\geq\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}=\bar q_\star(u)
\]
for every \(u\). Both \(x\mapsto\min\{\rho,x/t\}\) and \(x\mapsto1-x\) have the relevant monotonicities, so at every \(n\) and fixed start the void product generated by \(q'\) is no larger than \(\eta_n^\star\). Equivalently, its limiting hazard is at least \(H(a)\).

Now consider any two-sign late-void residual pair \(\widetilde r^+=g\), \(\widetilde r^-=-g\) with \(g=0\) on \([0,a']\), \(|g|\leq M\), and Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\). Continuity gives \(g(a')=0\), and hence, for \(u>a'\),
\[
 |g(u)|\leq\min\{L_r(u-a'),M\}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \left|2\int_0^1g(u)\,du\right|
 \leq2\int_0^1|g(u)|\,du
 \leq d(1-a'),
\]
with equality for the nonnegative clipped residual. If the limiting absolute causal separation is at least \(d\), strict monotonicity of \(d\) forces \(1-a'\geq x(d)\), or \(a'\leq a(d)\). Since \(H(a)\) strictly decreases and \(\exp\{-H(a)\}\) strictly increases with \(a\),
\[
 \exp\{-H(a')\}\leq\exp\{-H(a(d))\}.
\]
Together with pointwise intensity minimality, this proves the jointly optimized late-void envelope.

When \(L_q>c/2\), the analytic form of \(H(a(d))\) changes at \(a(d)=u_q\), equivalently at \(d=d(1-u_q)=d_q\). The residual analytic form changes at \(d=M^2/L_r\), which is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\). In that interior case,
\[
 \lim_{L_q\downarrow c/2}d\left(1-\frac{c}{2L_q}\right)=d(0)=0
 <\frac{M^2}{L_r},
\]
whereas
\[
 \lim_{L_q\to\infty}d\left(1-\frac{c}{2L_q}\right)=d(1)=d_{\max}
 >\frac{M^2}{L_r}.
\]
Thus admissible choices realize either ordering of the two interior elbows.

Finally, the required exact ramp is recovered by taking \(L_q=0\), \(c=a_\star=1/2\), \(L_r=1/2\), \(M\geq1/4\), and \(\rho\geq1/2\). Then \(\bar q_\star\equiv1/2\), \(g(u)=(u-1/2)_+/2\), and
\[
 d(1/2)=1/8,qquad
 [\exp\{-H(1/2)\}-2(0.05)]_+
 =\sqrt{1/2}-0.1=0.6071067811865475\ldots.
\]
For the complete enumeration at \(n=1,2,3,4\),
\[
 (\Delta_1,\Delta_2,\Delta_3,\Delta_4)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac14,\frac29,\frac3{16}\right),
 \qquad
 (\eta_1^\star,\eta_2^\star,\eta_3^\star,\eta_4^\star)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac34,\frac58,\frac{35}{48}\right).
\]
Every enumerated separation exceeds \(1/8\), and the void masses equal the exact assignment products. This all-confidence-set information calculation is separate from every Horvitz--Thompson or AIPW distributional limit.

added_lemmas.statement:
Every intensity-optimized clipped-ramp member lies in Li and Zhao's baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class and fails the negligible-increment requirement used for their Gaussian AIPW conclusion. Therefore every sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets that is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over that baseline class inherits, for every \(0<d<d_{\max}\) and each sign of the corresponding intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\geq d\}
 \geq[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+,
\]
where \(d_{\max}\), \(x(d)\), and \(H\) are those of the jointly optimized frontier theorem. Only this converse transfers by subclass inclusion. Neither the pair-specific attaining rule nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem is asserted on Li and Zhao's larger class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The sourced baseline-class node states the relevant published requirements. In the present construction,
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
Both probabilities are deterministic functions of every available history, strictly positive, strictly below one, and sum to one. The membership proposition proves that the potential outcomes are fixed and bounded and that the zero regression is predictable. Thus every member belongs to Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.

We verify the Gaussian obstruction directly. Write
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\},
 \qquad
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
The martingale increments are orthogonal by iterated conditioning. Therefore the variance of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error is
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^ng(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive at every \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\), while \(g(t/n)=0\) at all earlier indices. Hence
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n
 \frac{(t/n)g(t/n)^2}{\bar q_\star(t/n)}
 -\frac1{n^2}\sum_{t=1}^ng(t/n)^2
 \longrightarrow
 w_\star:=\int_{a_\star}^1
 \frac{u g(u)^2}{\bar q_\star(u)}\,du>0.
\]
The limit is finite because \(\bar q_\star\geq c/2\), and it is strictly positive because \(M,L_r>0\) and \(a_\star<1\).

At the unprojected two-arm-vector level, the control potential outcome and its regression are identically zero, so the AIPW covariance has a zero control row and column. Its smallest eigenvalue is zero, and the displayed Condition 3(ii) premise cannot hold. The obstruction is not merely this singular coordinate: it persists after projection to the nondegenerate treated contrast. Indeed, let \(q_1=\bar q_\star(1)\in[c/2,c]\) and \(g_1=g(1)>0\). At \(t=n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), the smallest binary assignment probability is \(q_1/n\), and the source's outcome-plus-regression envelope is at least \(g_1\). The scalar negligible-maximum analogue satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}
 \max_{1\leq t\leq n}
 \frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \geq\frac{g_1^2}{q_1^2w_\star}>0.
\]
It is not \(o(1)\), verifying that the late rare-arm increments remain nonnegligible even in the positive-variance projection.

Uniform honesty on Li and Zhao's baseline class implies honesty on this deterministic-propensity two-sign subclass. Applying the jointly optimized frontier theorem gives the displayed bound. This inclusion argument constructs no confidence procedure on the larger class, so it transfers neither exact attainment nor the positive structured-profile calibration theorem.

proposed_core_edits.name: qStar
proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires the intensity-minimizing profile to be a first-class object shared by the new family, its membership certificate, and the optimized frontier.

proposed.name: Intensity-optimized clipped-ramp family
proposed.construction:
Fix \(c>0\), \(L_q\geq0\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), \(a_\star\in(0,1)\), \(M>0\), \(L_r>0\), and \(K\geq c\). Define
\[
 \bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\},\qquad
 g_{a_\star}(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
For \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), put
\[
 \bar q^\sigma=\bar q_\star,\qquad
 r^\sigma(u)=\sigma g_{a_\star}(u),\qquad
 e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\},
\]
and set
\[
 m_{nt}(0)=m_{nt}(1)=0,qquad
 Y_{nt}^\sigma(0)=0,qquad
 Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)=r^\sigma(t/n).
\]
The sequential randomization law is \(\Pr_\sigma(A_{nt}=1\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=e_{nt}\), and the complete observation is \(O_n=(A_{n1:n},e_{n1:n},Y_{n1:n}^{\mathrm{obs}},m_{n1:n})\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Joint optimization requires a family using the pointwise-minimal admissible intensity together with the already certified clipped residual.

The residual-only frontier is a valid special case but is obsolete as the headline after the required joint optimization over the intensity class; the replacement preserves it at \(L_q=0\) and adds the intensity elbow.
The baseline-class transfer must track the jointly optimized witness while continuing to transfer only the converse.

proposed.comparator_claim: Definition 1 permits general positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, while Theorem 4(ii)'s Gaussian AIPW conclusion requires Condition 3, including its negligible-maximum part (ii).
Theorem 1 constructs doubly robust betting confidence sequences under predictable logging.
Proposition 1 proves selective type-I error control for the selective randomization p-value.
Theorem 1 proves asymptotic type-I error control for simulation with optimism in specified adaptive designs.
Proposition 2 gives an exact compound-Poisson law for an HT rate estimator under independent Poisson importance sampling.
Finite-population limited-overlap estimators are asymptotically Gaussian when their effective sample size diverges.
Any valid i.i.d. bounded-mean confidence interval obeys an inverse-information-projection width lower bound.
Stein perturbation yields explicit total-variation compound-Poisson approximation bounds for integer-valued sums.
Weighted Bernoulli and Poisson sums admit generalized Dickman approximation bounds.
Theorem 1 gives a semiparametrically efficient Gaussian limit for the truncated A2IPW estimator.
Resampling simulations find tighter superior-arm and wider inferior-arm intervals under real-time adaptive randomization.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Li--Zhao comparator now matches the joint intensity-and-residual frontier and its subclass-only converse transfer; all other comparator positions remain unchanged.

prose_updates.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe confidence interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, the pointwise-minimal admissible intensity \(\bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) and the capped clipped residual jointly optimize the all-confidence-set late-void converse: at \(0<d<d_{\max}\), honesty forces limiting large-diameter probability at least \([\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+\). The intensity elbow \(d_q=d(1-c/(2L_q))\), when \(L_q>c/2\), coexists in either order with the interior residual elbow \(M^2/L_r\). Exact attainment remains confined to each selected two-sign subexperiment, and subclass inclusion transfers only the converse to Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class. The original linear-ramp frontier, the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) result, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, and the high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain unchanged.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive-design class permits positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, but their Gaussian AIPW theorem requires a negligible-maximum condition that fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing adaptive and i.i.d. width results neither calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law nor optimize the complete-log common-void obstruction jointly over the declared intensity class \(\mathcal Q\) and the simultaneous \(M\)-bounded, \(L_r\)-Lipschitz residual constraints.
project_justification.niche: The boundary has two distinct deliverables. Structured deterministic profiles permit computable atom-safe positive calibration. For all-estimator information limits, \(\bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) is the pointwise-smallest admissible intensity and the capped clipped ramp saturates \(\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\); together they produce a joint late-void probability--diameter envelope with separate intensity and residual elbows.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the declared structured subclass, plus an exact finite-sample tradeoff for each intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair and the jointly optimized asymptotic envelope \([\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+\). A sourced subclass-inclusion argument lifts only that converse to Li and Zhao's larger baseline binary adaptive class. Pairwise attainment, positive calibration, the original linear frontier, the exact ramp certificate, and the high-hazard radius retain their separately stated scopes.

prose_updates.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their baseline binary class contains the deterministic intensity-optimized clipped ramps, but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; these bounded-hazard witnesses fail its negligible-maximum part because late standardized increments remain nonnegligible. The present joint intensity-and-residual converse therefore transfers by subclass inclusion, while its matching confidence-set construction remains sharp only inside each selected two-sign subexperiment and the positive profile-net theorem remains confined to this note's structured subclass. Bibaut and Kallus (2025) organize adaptive inference into Gaussian repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) provide predictable-logging confidence sequences, Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026) study selection-conditioned randomization tests, and Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) invert simulated adaptive laws; none supplies this finite-population signed atomic calibration or the jointly optimized common-void envelope. Chen et al. (2026) obtain a compound-Poisson HT law under independent Poisson importance sampling, while Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat limited overlap with diverging effective information. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds rather than the present exact sequential two-sign tradeoff. Barbour and Xia (1999) support compound-Poisson error accounting, and Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for GUSTO-1 and EUROPA.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete experiments, and therefore does not imply the all-estimator lower bound. The joint frontier instead uses an exact common subprobability on a late-arm void event. Its intensity certificate is pointwise optimal only for deterministic designs of the stated form generated from \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and its residual certificate is optimal only within the declared late-void two-sign witness geometry under the existing \(M,L_r\) constraints. The matching procedure knows the selected pair, so it establishes no global minimax attainment over the full structured class. Subclass inclusion transfers the converse, but neither attainment nor positive calibration, to Li and Zhao's baseline class. The positive theorem still requires fixed profiles, deterministic domination for same-log threshold selection, and supplied profile and early-variation contracts. The \(0.442M\) high-hazard result remains a subfamily upper bound. The polynomial bit-complexity question remains open because the pruning invariant gives no polynomial bound on the number of profile boxes straddling the certification boundary.

Exact attainment is only for each selected two-sign intensity-optimized clipped-ramp subexperiment; no global minimax attainment is claimed for the structured class or Li and Zhao's larger baseline class. The positive profile-net theorem, the original linear-ramp frontier, the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) diagnostic, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard result keep their prior scopes.
